decisionsTitle: «Punctele, pe scurt»: the points of «Planul voluntarilor» as one table at the top — the route by kilometre, then the start–finish — printed first as the plan's summary sheet (amending §952)
decisionsSection:
**The owner, 2026-11-17, four days before Saturday's race, on «Planul voluntarilor»:** «aș vrea să văd punctele ca și tabel, mai ales pe traseu».

**What was there.** Each point of the plan is a card of its own (§949, §961): its title, what it is, its coordinates and «Deschide pe hartă», the people placed there with their telephones, «Pune aici» and the fold «Modifică punctul». The whole plan was a scroll through every card, past the picture, «Punctele planului» and «Trimite fiecăruia punctul lui», which stand between the title and the first card.

**Decision.** A section «Punctele, pe scurt» / "The points at a glance" right under the page's title and intro — after «Tipărește planul», before the picture and the cards — under a level-3 heading like the page's other sections, with the house's list glyph (the one «Înscrieri» wears). It holds one table of every point of the plan, six columns:

- «Nr.» — the plan's own number (`listPlanPoints`), empty at the start–finish;
- «Punct» — the point's name in the page's language, a link to its card below (`#point-<id>`, the id the cards already had);
- «Km» — the kilometre as the card's title writes it («4,5»), or «start–finish», the plan's word the «Voluntari» list uses;
- «Coordonate» — the numbers (`formatCoordinates`) with the card's «Deschide pe hartă» beside them (Google Maps, a new tab), «—» when the point has none;
- «Voluntari» — the people the card shows, in the card's order, each on a line of their own with the telephone as the card's `tel:` link (the digits and the plus, read grouped), «niciunul» / "nobody" where nobody stands;
- «Câți» — how many stand there.

Under the table one line totals it: «{n} voluntari puși, {m} puncte fără nimeni», each number a counted phrase (`countForm`; the second is the summary's own «puncte fără nimeni»).

**The order: the route first.** «Mai ales pe traseu»: the route's points come first, in the plan's one order — by kilometre, which is the order `listPlanPoints` numbers them in, so by number too; a point the organizers typed last stands where its kilometre puts it, as on their map. Then the start–finish points, as the page lists them (the order they were added). The cards below keep their own order, the start–finish group first.

**Read from what the page already reads.** No new query, not even a grouped one: the rows are the plan's points as `readVolunteerPlan` returns them, the very objects the cards are drawn from, so a row says what its card says. The telephone dials what the card dials — one function now, `dialOf`, for both. Nobody sees anything new: the same page behind the same gate (`canManageVolunteers`: the Organizer and the Administrators; anybody else gets the 404 of an address that does not exist).

**The house's table.** `AdminTable`, as the «Voluntari» list: a table from `md` up, below it a block a point headed by the point's name (the «Nr.» line left out at the start–finish, where there is no number), with the columns' widths and «Coloane» every backoffice table has. Two things it never had to do, added as opt-ins that every other list leaves off, so every list reads and prints as it did:

- `paged={false}` — every row on the one page: no rows-per-page links and no pager, which here would only reload the same page;
- `printable` — on paper the wide table whatever the sheet's width (an A4 sheet is narrower than `md`, where the screen draws the blocks), never the blocks or their hints, and nothing to press: the columns' edges, «Coloane», the widths' reset, the page sizes, the pager.

Every link of the table is a thumb's 44 pixels — a point's name, a telephone, «Deschide pe hartă» (BR-REQ-041-01 criterion 6).

**On paper (amending §952).** The table is the plan's summary sheet: printed whole, as a table, the first thing after the sheet's title — the map's links left off, the names and the telephones as text. The picture, which §952 made the first thing after the title, is now the first thing after the table, still in one piece and at most 17 cm tall. The cards keep their own print rules.

**Nothing else moves.** The cards and their forms, the picture, «Punctele planului», «Trimite fiecăruia punctul lui», the summary line above the cards, «Fără punct», the addresses, the actions and who may open the page are what they were. A plan with no point has no table: the list's own empty state says how to add one.

**Refused.**

- *A table drawn by hand, as the emergency sheet's.* Six columns at 320 pixels are a sideways scroll over somebody's name; the house's table turns into a block a point on a phone and resizes like every list.
- *The page sizes left under it, as the newsletter's history keeps them.* Links that reload the same page are noise on the plan and on its paper.
- *The table in place of the cards.* The cards carry the presses — «Pune aici», «Scoate», «Modifică punctul» — which the owner did not ask to move.
- *A page break after the table on paper.* The picture already goes to the next sheet when it does not fit under the table — it is never cut — and a forced break would cost a sheet whenever it does fit.

**Not done.** Editing in the table; sorting or filtering it; an export of it (the «Voluntari» list's Excel has the points); the public pages.
changelogLine: - **«Punctele, pe scurt» on «Planul voluntarilor»** — every point of the plan in one table at the top: the route by kilometre, then the start–finish, each with its number, its name (a link to its card), its kilometre, its coordinates and map link, the volunteers placed there with their telephones and how many, and a total of the people placed and the points with nobody; a block a point on a phone, and printed first, as a table. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Amends criterion 235 in what comes first on paper. Given the page `/admin/events/[id]/plan-voluntari` of an event whose plan has points, then right under the title and its intro — after «Tipărește planul» and before the picture, «Punctele planului», «Trimite fiecăruia punctul lui» and the points' cards — a section «Punctele, pe scurt» / "The points at a glance" (`#plan-table`, a level-3 heading with the list's glyph) holds one table of every point of the plan in six columns, «Nr.» / "No.", «Punct» / "Point", «Km», «Coordonate» / "Coordinates", «Voluntari» / "Volunteers" and «Câți» / "How many": the route's points first, in the plan's order — by kilometre, and so by number — then the start–finish points as the page lists them. A row says the point's number (none at the start–finish); its name in the page's language, a link to its card (`#point-<id>`); its kilometre as the card writes it, or «start–finish»; its coordinates with «Deschide pe hartă» (a new tab), or «—»; the people its card shows, in the card's order, each on a line with their telephone as a `tel:` link of the digits and the plus, or «niciunul» / "nobody"; and how many. One line under the table says the people placed and the points with nobody, each a counted phrase in both languages («5 voluntari puși, 2 puncte fără nimeni»). The rows are the plan the cards are drawn from; nothing else of the page changes; a plan with no point has no table; and the page is the same 404 for every role that may not work the volunteers. On paper the table is printed whole, as a table, the first thing after the sheet's title — its map links left off, its names and telephones as text — and the picture comes after it, in one piece (2026-11-17, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given `/admin/events/[id]/plan-voluntari` on a 320-pixel screen and on a desktop, then «Punctele, pe scurt» is a block a point on the phone — headed by the point's name, with no «Nr.» line at the start–finish — and a table of six columns on the desktop; nothing of the page is wider than the screen; every link of it — a point's name, a telephone, «Deschide pe hartă» — is at least 44 pixels tall; a point's name brings its card into view; and printed on either screen, the table is drawn as a table while the blocks, the map's links and the table's controls are not. Verification: e2e `volunteer-plan-mail.spec.ts` under both Playwright viewport projects (2026-11-17, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given a backoffice table, then it pages through its address and prints as the browser lays it out unless it is asked otherwise: asked `paged={false}`, it draws no rows-per-page links and no pager and keeps the line under the table; asked `printable`, on paper it draws the wide table whatever the sheet's width — after the screen's rule that hides it under `md` — and never the phone's blocks or their hints, nor a column's edge, «Coloane», the widths' reset, the page sizes or the pager; a table asked neither carries no print rule of its own (2026-11-17, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

batchLine: the plan's points as one table at the top of «Planul voluntarilor», printed first
